brewing.notes: A safe starting point for dark tea: rinse once, boiling water, or simmer it the traditional way.

description:
A reprocessed compressed tea from Ningqiang county in Hanzhong, Shaanxi, made from local green tea stock.

Treat it as you would any dark tea: rinse it, use boiling water, and buy from someone who can say who pressed it and when.
history: It is a recent product line of a Hanzhong tea company, which lists it among its own named teas and holds a patent on making brick tea from Shaanxi green tea. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Baked and pan-fired raw green tea from the Ningqiang area is treated to reduce bitterness and astringency, then refined and pressed.
harvest_season: Often made from coarser, later leaf, as with most dark teas.
appearance_dry: A tight, even brick of blue-brown colour.
appearance_wet: Usually coarse dark leaf with some stem.
taste_profile: Clean aroma and a mellow, full taste; holds up to repeated steeping.
vintage_note: Dark teas are sold by production year and many improve with several years of dry storage.
